LANDING.HERO_DESC: Production-style chat built with Angular 21 and a Go API gateway: OAuth at the edge, async Gemini streaming over SSE, file attachments via Azure Blob, a searchable model picker, and durable threads you can rename or delete. Postgres is the source of truth; Redis carries live chunks; NATS coordinates orphan file cleanup when a conversation goes away.
LANDING.CARD_ANGULAR: Angular 21 with signals, strict TypeScript, Module Federation into the shell, and split chat clients (`MessageService`, `MessageStreamService`, `ConversationService`, `ChatModelService`) aligned to gateway routes.
LANDING.CARD_PRIMENG: PrimeNG 21 + Aura for shell layout, dialogs, and confirmations; chat uses a Claude-style composer with a custom searchable model menu (not a stock `p-select` overlay).
LANDING.CARD_AUTH: angular-oauth2-oidc with PKCE; Google and Microsoft sign-in via the Go gateway, which issues short-lived internal JWTs — the browser never holds `client_secret`.
LANDING.CARD_API: chatbot-service (FastAPI): Postgres-first messages, Redis queue + SSE streams, `GET /models`, JetStream `chatbot.message.sent` (and outbox retry), `DELETE /conversations` with orphan-safe `conversation.deleted`.
LANDING.CARD_POSTGRES: chatbot-service Postgres: conversations, messages, `message_files`, `event_outbox`. file-service Postgres: blob metadata per owner. Alembic owns schema in each service.
LANDING.CARD_REDIS: Job queue (`chatbot:jobs`) and per-job streams (`chatbot:events:{job_id}`) so any API replica can replay SSE; clients resume with `Last-Event-ID`.
LANDING.CARD_GEMINI: Worker calls the model from your picker (`streamGenerateContent`); sidebar titles use Gemini Flash Lite. Optional `CHAT_MODEL_ALLOWLIST`; API key only on chatbot-service.
LANDING.CARD_I18N: @ngx-translate JSON catalogs (en/de); locale maps to `Accept-Language` on every gateway-proxied API call.
LANDING.CARD_GATEWAY: Go API gateway: OAuth token exchange, internal JWT, `stream_token` on `POST /messages`, reverse proxy to chatbot, files, and event-store APIs.
LANDING.CARD_FILE_SERVICE: Fastify: SAS prepare → browser PUT to Azure → confirm in Postgres; publishes `file.uploaded`; consumes `conversation.deleted` for orphan blob cleanup.
LANDING.CARD_EVENT_STORE: TypeScript service: pull ingest from JetStream `EVENTS` into Postgres — `chatbot.message.sent`, `file.uploaded`, `conversation.deleted`, and related platform subjects.
LANDING.CARD_AZURE_BLOB: Attachment bytes in Azure Blob; SAS URLs for browser upload and server-side delete. chatbot-service stores `file_id` refs only — never proxies file bytes.
LANDING.CARD_NATS: JetStream stream `EVENTS`: `file.uploaded`, `chatbot.message.sent`, `conversation.deleted` (and `file.deleted`). Topology from platform-nats; outbox when publish fails.

FLOWS.PICKER_ARIA: Choose which flow diagram to explore

FLOW.TITLE: How a message moves
FLOW.SUBTITLE: Click a block for detail. Happy path: attach files (optional) via SAS into Azure Blob → pick a Gemini model → send. Platform events (`file.uploaded`, `chatbot.message.sent`) go to JetStream for audit; chat latency stays on Postgres + Redis + SSE.
FLOW.DIAGRAM_ARIA: Chatbot architecture flow: select a step to read details
FLOW.EVENTS_NOTE: NATS publishes are async and non-blocking — failed publishes land in each service's Postgres outbox until the broker is back.
FLOW.LOOP_NOTE: FastAPI uses XREAD on the Redis Stream `chatbot:events:{job_id}` and forwards chunks as SSE — safe with multiple API replicas because the stream is shared Redis state, not stuck in one process.
FLOW.PANEL_EMPTY: Tap a step: Angular, gateway, chatbot-service, file-service, Azure Blob, NATS, event-store, Postgres, Redis, worker, or Azure DevOps.

ANGULAR.TITLE: Angular 21 (browser)
ANGULAR.DESC: Login, home, and chat UI — HttpClient + EventSource for streamed replies; can run standalone or as a shell remote.
ANGULAR.D1: Strict TypeScript, standalone components, signals for local UI state.
ANGULAR.D3: PrimeNG 21 + Aura: toolbar, cards, confirmation dialogs, theme tokens.
ANGULAR.D4: angular-oauth2-oidc with PKCE; token exchange only via the Go gateway.
ANGULAR.D5: Route guards + APP_INITIALIZER so OIDC finishes before protected routes.
ANGULAR.D6: Chat API clients grouped by route: messages, streams, conversations, models.
ANGULAR.D7: Composer: SAS file attachments, Claude-style input card, searchable model picker (localStorage preference).
ANGULAR.D8: Sidebar: paginated history, rename, delete with confirm, open thread.

FASTAPI.TITLE: FastAPI (chatbot-service)
FASTAPI.DESC: HTTP boundary for chat and models — auth and CORS live at the gateway.
FASTAPI.D1: Routers for conversations, messages, stream, and `GET /models`.
FASTAPI.D2: Postgres first: persist the user message (and file refs) before enqueueing.
FASTAPI.D3: Push job to Redis with owner, model id, correlation id, and attachment descriptors.
FASTAPI.D4: SSE handler XREADs the job stream; enriches `done` with conversation title from Postgres.
FASTAPI.D5: JWT + `X-Owner-ID` from the gateway — no Google credentials in this service.
FASTAPI.D6: User messages store `file_id` references only — bytes stay in Azure Blob via file-service.
FASTAPI.D7: `GET /models` proxies Google `models.list` (filtered) for the UI picker.
FASTAPI.D8: After the durable user write: publish `events.chatbot.message.sent` (`type`: `chatbot.message.sent`, role user).
FASTAPI.D9: Failed JetStream publish → `event_outbox` row; API drain retries to stream `EVENTS`.

POSTGRES.TITLE: PostgreSQL
POSTGRES.DESC: System of record for conversations, message rows, and completed assistant text + metadata (or failure state).
POSTGRES.D1: Relational model for threads and ordered messages; migrations for schema evolution.
POSTGRES.D2: Assistant completion written when the stream ends — Redis chunks are not the sole truth.
POSTGRES.D3: Async SQLAlchemy (or equivalent) from the same service codebase as the API.

REDIS.TITLE: Redis
REDIS.DESC: Decouple long model runs from the HTTP request: queue jobs via BLPOP and deliver live chunks over Redis Streams.
REDIS.D1: Job queue (`chatbot:jobs`): BLPOP so POST /messages returns quickly after the durable Postgres write.
REDIS.D2: Redis Streams (`chatbot:events:{job_id}`): worker XADDs chunks; FastAPI XREADs and forwards to SSE clients.
REDIS.D3: Last-Event-ID reconnect: each SSE event carries the stream entry ID; XREAD resumes from that ID on reconnect — no data loss.

WORKER.TITLE: Worker + Google AI
WORKER.DESC: Background process: stream the selected Gemini model and publish chunks to Redis.
WORKER.D1: Separate process from Uvicorn — scale and deploy independently.
WORKER.D2: `streamGenerateContent` with the job's model id (your picker choice).
WORKER.D3: XADD incremental chunks; persist full assistant text to Postgres on completion.
WORKER.D4: Loads attachment bytes from file-service (Azure Blob behind SAS download) for multimodal turns.
WORKER.D5: Sidebar titles via `generateContent` on Gemini Flash Lite after the first reply.
WORKER.D6: Enqueues `chatbot.message.sent` (assistant) to outbox after persisting the full reply — same subject as the API user event.

ADO.TITLE: Azure DevOps
ADO.DESC: Each service is its own repo with YAML pipelines (build, test, bot-review with Gemini).
ADO.D1: Separate ADO repos: gateway, chatbot-service, file-service, frontends, platform-nats, event-store.
ADO.D2: PR pipelines: unit tests, MegaLinter, optional PR-Agent review.
ADO.D3: Variable groups for secrets; deploy order respects NATS topology before consumers.

GATEWAY.TITLE: API Gateway (Go)
GATEWAY.DESC: Single browser entry point: OAuth, JWT, proxy, and stream tokens.
GATEWAY.D1: Google OAuth exchange — holds `client_secret`; browser never sends it downstream.
GATEWAY.D2: Issues internal JWTs for the browser after OAuth; downstream services never verify JWT.
GATEWAY.D3: Validates Bearer JWT at the edge and injects `X-Owner-ID` on every proxied route.
GATEWAY.D4: Adds `stream_token` to `POST /messages` for scoped SSE access.

FILE_SERVICE.TITLE: File Service (Fastify)
FILE_SERVICE.DESC: Orchestrates chat attachments: Postgres metadata, Azure Blob bytes, gateway auth.
FILE_SERVICE.D1: `POST /files/prepare` returns a `file_id` and short-lived SAS URL for upload.
FILE_SERVICE.D2: `POST /files/confirm` persists name, size, MIME, owner, and blob path after the PUT succeeds.
FILE_SERVICE.D3: Chat `POST /messages` sends `file_id` references — not raw file bytes.
FILE_SERVICE.D4: Trusted `X-Owner-ID` from the gateway on prepare, confirm, and download.
FILE_SERVICE.D5: Serves SAS download to the worker when Gemini needs inline attachment data.
FILE_SERVICE.D6: On confirm: publish `events.file.file.uploaded` (`type`: `file.uploaded`) with standard envelope.

AZURE_BLOB.TITLE: Azure Blob Storage
AZURE_BLOB.DESC: Where attachment bytes live — browser uploads directly; services read back through file-service.
AZURE_BLOB.D1: Composer upload: browser PUTs to the SAS URL from prepare (no byte proxy through chatbot-service).
AZURE_BLOB.D2: Blob container and path are stored on the file row at confirm time.
AZURE_BLOB.D3: Worker multimodal path reads the same object via file-service — Gemini never gets long-lived SAS URLs.

NATS.TITLE: NATS JetStream
NATS.DESC: Shared `EVENTS` stream for cross-service audit — chat UX does not wait on these publishes.
NATS.D1: `events.file.file.uploaded` from file-service after a successful confirm.
NATS.D2: `events.chatbot.message.sent` from chatbot-service API after the user message is in Postgres.
NATS.D3: `events.chatbot.message.sent` again from the worker (assistant role) after the stream completes — often via outbox enqueue.

EVENT_STORE.TITLE: Event Store
EVENT_STORE.DESC: Pull consumer ingests `events.chatbot.>` and `events.file.>` from JetStream into Postgres for query and replay.
EVENT_STORE.D1: Ingests `file.uploaded` and `chatbot.message.sent` alongside other platform subjects.
EVENT_STORE.D2: Retention and query APIs are separate from chatbot-service operational tables.
EVENT_STORE.D3: DLQ traffic (`events.dlq.>`) is not stored as normal business events.

DELETE_FLOW.TITLE: How delete works
DELETE_FLOW.SUBTITLE: Deleting a chat is synchronous for Postgres and the HTTP response; Azure Blob cleanup is async. Only file IDs that no other conversation still references are published — attachments shared across threads stay intact.
DELETE_FLOW.DIAGRAM_ARIA: Conversation delete flow: select a step to read details
DELETE_FLOW.NOTE: The API returns 204 as soon as Postgres commits. file-service soft-deletes metadata, removes bytes from Azure Blob Storage, and event-store ingests the envelope in the background; failed publishes can drain from the outbox later.
DELETE_FLOW.PANEL_EMPTY: Tap a step: Angular confirm, gateway, chatbot-service, Postgres, NATS, file-service, Azure Blob, or event-store.

ANGULAR.TITLE: Angular 21 (browser)
ANGULAR.DESC: Chat UI issues delete after confirm; the browser does not wait for Azure Blob or NATS cleanup.
ANGULAR.D1: Delete chat control on the active thread (sidebar menu / trash).
ANGULAR.D2: PrimeNG confirmation dialog before any network call.
ANGULAR.D4: On 204, remove the thread from local state and navigate away if it was open.

GATEWAY.TITLE: API Gateway (Go)
GATEWAY.DESC: Forwards the delete with the same JWT and owner headers as every other chat route.
GATEWAY.D1: Validates internal JWT on the proxied DELETE.
GATEWAY.D2: Injects `X-Owner-ID` and `X-Correlation-ID` for orphan scoping and tracing.
GATEWAY.D3: Reverse-proxies to chatbot-service; no conversation rows live in the gateway.

FASTAPI.TITLE: FastAPI (chatbot-service)
FASTAPI.DESC: Owns the delete transaction, orphan `file_id` list, and NATS publish (or outbox).
FASTAPI.D1: Before delete: SQL finds `file_id`s on this thread not referenced by any other conversation for the same owner (`NOT EXISTS`).
FASTAPI.D2: Deletes the conversation; cascade removes messages and `message_files` rows, then commits.
FASTAPI.D3: After commit: publish `events.chatbot.conversation.deleted` with standard envelope + `payload.file_ids` (orphans only).
FASTAPI.D4: If JetStream is down: row goes to Postgres `event_outbox`; API drain retries later.
FASTAPI.D5: Responds 204 immediately — never blocks on file-service or blob deletion.

POSTGRES.TITLE: PostgreSQL
POSTGRES.DESC: Authoritative removal of the thread; publish only happens after a successful commit.
POSTGRES.D1: `message_files` links messages to `file_id`s used for orphan detection.
POSTGRES.D2: FK cascade drops messages and links when the conversation row goes away.
POSTGRES.D3: Failed deletes roll back — no NATS event on error.

NATS.TITLE: NATS JetStream
NATS.DESC: Carries the platform event so file-service and event-store can react without coupling HTTP.
NATS.D3: Empty `file_ids` is valid when the thread had no attachments or every file is still used elsewhere.

FILE_SERVICE.TITLE: File Service (Fastify)
FILE_SERVICE.DESC: Pull consumer orchestrates orphan cleanup: Postgres metadata first, then Azure Blob bytes.
FILE_SERVICE.D2: For each `file_id`: match envelope `owner_id` to the file row in file-service Postgres.
FILE_SERVICE.D3: Soft-delete the metadata row after ownership checks pass.
FILE_SERVICE.D4: Call Azure Blob Storage SDK to delete the object at the stored blob path.
FILE_SERVICE.D5: Emits `events.file.file.deleted` per successful removal; duplicate delivery → log and ack.

AZURE_BLOB.TITLE: Azure Blob Storage
AZURE_BLOB.DESC: Attachment bytes live here — upload uses SAS from the browser; delete is server-side from file-service.
AZURE_BLOB.D1: Each confirmed file row stores the blob container/path used at upload time.
AZURE_BLOB.D2: Orphan cleanup removes the object after the Postgres soft-delete succeeds.
AZURE_BLOB.D3: Upload path never proxies bytes through chatbot-service; delete path never blocks the user's 204.

EVENT_STORE.TITLE: Event Store
EVENT_STORE.DESC: Ingests the same JetStream message for audit and replay — does not drive user-visible delete.
EVENT_STORE.D1: Pull ingest from `EVENTS` per platform topology.
EVENT_STORE.D2: Stores the envelope for operators and downstream analytics.
EVENT_STORE.D3: DLQ subjects are not ingested as normal business events.
